comment: Known disagreements scripts/formal/refdiff-harness.py --ci accepts (none since #187: the Q1 rule, a content-free alias loop compared as a literal $ref, went with the name-keyed cut). Each rule names the harness classes it covers; `pointer` (exact), `pointer_suffix` and `verdict`, when present, must match the record (`verdict`: both records'); `requires: alias-loop` is checked by the harness (q1_checker): the record's use must reach, on either side, a component in an alias loop or leading into one that is named by the record's ref: values or its counterpart's at the same use, owner and pointer, or by its owner pair when that component is a pure alias ({$ref} and nothing else after canonicalisation); and the node at the record's owner-relative pointer without /$ref must, on one side, be an object whose $ref names an alias-loop component. formal/refdiff/negative/ holds corruptions this must reject. See formal/README.md, "Reference semantics of `$ref` diffs", Known limits.
